chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali b. Mahziyar who said: I wrote to Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, should I pray behind the one who says 'the body' (God is corporeal), or the one who says the saying of Yunus - meaning Ibn Abd al-Rahman? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Do not pray behind them nor give them from the Zakat, and disassociate from them. Allah has disassociated from them.

key_terms.الْجَسَمِ: Corporeality (doctrine that God has a physical body)
key_terms.يُونُسَ: Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman, a prominent early Shia theologian whose doctrine was debated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind those who believe in God's corporeality according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Saduq’s *Al-Majalis* highlights the theological criterion of 'al-Jasad' (corporeality) and the specific doctrine of Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman as markers of deviation warranting religious disassociation (*ibra'*). The Imam’s ruling extends beyond mere prayer validity to include financial ties (Zakat) and communal separation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on purifying the community from those who anthropomorphize God or hold distinct erroneous beliefs. This establishes a precedent for evaluating the theological orthodoxy of prayer leaders in early Shia communities.
